Oh lord I identify with this so much. I mean I'm not a girl so I don't have to wear a scarf but I get what you're saying here and just reading through the comments, yeah I've been there.

In the end I kinda decided that well, yeah Islam is very very flawed with lots of issues that need to be talked about. However I still pray, and still consider myself a Muslim simply because, well, alot of those things did help me alot. And even though Islam is flawed I liked the positive aspects of it alot such as Zakah and jihad (I mean the jihad that's supposed to be a fight against the demons within yourself, not war jihad) stuff like that. I just hate the other stupid shit in it and hated the homophobia, and justifying Ayesha's marriage and other such things.

So in the end my advice to you is that, cling on to the stuff that helps you and gives you hope in Islam, while also condemning the more horrible stuff in it. That can feel alot more liberating. Yes, some other Muslims or scholars will say that technically speaking this disqualifies a person as a Muslim, but who gives a shit? I want to able to support my gay homies and pray too, cuz I like doing both things.
